title: Shortbread Biscuits
subtitle: Crisp, buttery Scottish shortbread
excerpt: Shortbread needs only three ingredients and rewards a light hand. The dough chills before baking so the biscuits hold their shape. They keep well in a tin for over a week.
sourceNotes: Shortbread originates in Scotland and was historically associated with festive occasions. Mary Queen of Scots is said to have been fond of the biscuit, and it has remained a Scottish staple for centuries.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked biscuits in a sealed container for up to 3 months. Thaw at room temperature.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch and freeze half unbaked. Slice from frozen and add 2 minutes to the bake time.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dough log can be wrapped and refrigerated for up to 3 days before slicing and baking.

content.text: Work the dough until it just comes together. Overworking develops the gluten and makes the biscuits tough rather than crumbly.
Put the flour and butter in a bowl. Rub together with your fingertips until the mix resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Squeeze the crumbs together until a dough forms. Do not add water.
Shape into a log about 5cm in diameter. Wrap in cling film.
Heat the oven to 160C. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Slice the log into rounds about 7mm thick. Place on the tray with a little space between each.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until pale gold at the edges. They should not brown deeply.
Leave to cool on the tray for 5 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool fully.

items.symptom: Biscuits spread and lose their shape.
items.cause: Butter was too warm or dough was not chilled long enough.
items.fix: Chill the sliced rounds for 10 minutes before baking.
Mix only until the dough just comes together, then stop.

items.symptom: Biscuits are pale and soft after cooling.
items.cause: Underbaked. Shortbread firms on cooling but must be set through.
items.fix: Add 3 more minutes and check that edges are lightly golden.
